plain: To pay the cost of something.

webster.text: To pay; to discharge, as cost or expense; to bear, as charge, cost or expense.

more.text: To satisfy; as, to defray anger.
To fill; as, to defray a bottle.

example.quote: For forty years we have laid duties on tobacco, to defray the expenses of the inspection, and to raise an incidental revenue for the state.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 17, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
